correctness.rationale: For every even integer p>=4, H=v^p/p+u^2-u^3/3 has zero polynomial derivative along the system. The compact energy oval exists exactly for 0<h<4/3. Exact time quadratures I_k give T=2p^(-alpha)I_0 and drift=I_1/I_0-1; the integrated dot v identity gives I_2=2I_1. Scaled beta integrals prove small-energy T and drift. At h=4/3-delta, factorization 4/3-V=(u+1)(2-u)^2/3 and integrable saddle scaling give delta^beta I_0 -> B(1/p,beta)/2; the separately finite weighted limit J -> 3^(2/p)B(1/p,2/p) fixes the saddle drift constant. The drift is real analytic in the open annulus, negative near 0 and positive near 4/3, implying a nonempty finite zero set, and its period minimum is attained. Other projected energy components have no closed curves, and projected equilibria give nonzero axial translation. Symbolic and numerical package checker replay returns CHECK_OK; its finite tests are not the proof of infinite assertions.

The accessible Fonda–Garrione–Sfecci (2026) separated-variable period theory assumes global center in its principal framework, which fails here, and does not discuss the axial drift. Published mathematical searches and current/preceding-week claim deduplication expose no dominating combined statement. value.rationale: The natural higher even-kinetic degeneration of the 2022 polynomial periodic-cylinder example creates two physically different singular period boundaries. Exact beta-function coefficients and first drift corrections quantify both, and the drift changes sign to force a finite, nonempty collection of invariant three-dimensional cylinders entirely foliated by periodic orbits. This relates mathematical geometry and original-time observations of a canonical polynomial skew flow; it goes beyond the known p=2 qualitative cylinder result and is neither a textbook variable renaming nor an arbitrary numerical cutoff.
